en:
Or maybe they're already here.
When you turn around, {a}, right behind you...{p}

Just kidding.
Kidding, kidding.
Okay, before I tell the last story, I'll introduce myseeelf.
I'm Reiko Fukuzawa, from Class 1-G.
I'm a first-year, same as you, {a}.
Nice to meet you.{p}
Hey, so, {a}, are you the type who believes in superstitions?
I believe in them
I don't believe in them

Oh, really.
You do have that kind of personality, huh.
Then I bet you're the type who believes in fortune-telling too.
But you know, you can't totally laugh that stuff off.
Most of it's kind of a joke, but a lot of it makes you go, yeah, yeah, that's so true.
Still, you'd better not overdo it.
If you get too into it, you'll end up like the girl I'm about to tell you about...{p}

Actually, my big sister used to go to this school too.
So this is a story I heard from my sister. One of her classmates was a girl named Kanae Hirai.
She was a serious girl, but apparently she wanted to get married way, way more than normal.
And she was still only in high school.{p}
Hey, hey, {a}, do you want to get married young?
I do
Not really
If I meet the right person

...That's a safe answer.
Well, sure, if you meet the right person, anybody would want to.
And I guess it was the same with her, but thing is, she wanted to get married sooo badly, right?
And on top of that, her standards were sky-high.{p}

Everybody has their ideals, I guess, but you shouldn't aim too high.
I mean, even I don't aim too high.
If I had to name something, he'd be cool, and kind, and have money, and be able to do laundry, and be a great cook... that's about it.
I'm not picky about which school he went to or his family background.
Hey, hey, {a}, what's your ideal type?{p}If you had to rank them, tell me which one you'd put first.
Looks
Personality
Being good at housework

Ooh, so personality comes first.
So you don't care at all what their face looks like, huh.
Ehehe... just kidding, just kidding.{p}Okay, so what comes next?
Looks
Being good at housework

Oh, really.
So the next most important thing is housework.
So, like, you'd want your wife to be able to cook and do the laundry and stuff?
You want her to make you yummy meals and keep the house spick-and-span all the time?
But you know, that kind of thing isn't good.
That's acting like a bossy husband who lords it over the house.
Nobody does that kind of thing these days.
Nowadays, it's way more in style for the guy to do the cooking and the cleaning.
If you keep being so selfish and can't even cook a meal, nobody's going to want to marry you.
Well, but personality matters more to you, right?
So you could forgive her even if she's not that great at housework.
...Which means looks really don't matter to you after all.
If she's got a good personality, cooks well, loves cleaning and does your laundry, then even if she's ugly, she's perfect, right?
I think I'm kind of starting to figure you out, {a}.{p}

...But really, you'd hate it if she weren't good-looking too, right?
Whatever you say, you still want her face and her figure to be above average, don't you?{p}

It's fine, it's fine, you don't have to hide it.
Guys are all like that anyway.
It's good to have ideals on the high side.
You know how some people say anyone would be fine? Those are exactly the people whose standards are crazy-high.
You're cute by comparison, {a}.
Especially compared to that Hirai girl.{p}

Honestly, when I heard about Hirai, I was really shocked.
I mean, she had it all decided, from the guy's name right down to his age.
Can you believe that?
It's crazy.
His name, right?
His birthday, right?
His blood type, right?
Where he was born, right?
That's the kind of stuff she was fixated on.
She put those things before personality or looks.
Weird thing to be fixated on, huh?
And besides, it's not like you can just run into someone like that so easily.
But Hirai truly believed she'd meet him.
And she believed she'd be able to marry him before she turned twenty.
What she based that on, I have no idea.
But apparently that's what her fortune said.
Hirai was born under that kind of star, she said.
Supposedly some super-famous fortune-teller told her that when she was in grade school.
Whoever told her that is just as bad.
I like fortune-telling too, but I don't really believe in it.
For me, it's half just for fun.
But believing a fortune from grade school all the way into high school, and searching for that person the whole time, that's sooo romantic.
It's kinda scary, but it's still romantic, right?
I think so, anyway.
Because I could never go that far.
Of course, she never found anyone like that, so she was still searching even in high school.{p}

It was intense, I heard.
When Hirai started here, she looked up the names of everyone, from her classmates to the seniors.
Apparently there were a bunch of people with the same surname, or with names that were read the same but written differently.
Well, sure, with a school as big as this one.
But even if the name matched, there's still his blood type and his birthday and everything, right?
There's no way she'd ever find him.
Her friends who knew what was going on all laughed about it, apparently.
But Hirai had this eerie, desperate intensity about her, so nobody ever said it out loud.{p}

The school festival was supposedly insane.
They say she went around asking every single boy who came over from other schools what his name was.
Apparently some guy thought it was funny and lied to her as a joke, but it came out later.
And he nearly got killed by Hirai, they say.
It caused a huge uproar, apparently.
Scary, huh?{p}

Even so, there's no way Hirai would give up.
She kept on searching, on and on and on.
But her deadline was twenty, right?
If she didn't marry her destined one by twenty, she'd never be happy.
Worse than that, she even believed she would die.
As if that could ever happen.
But she'd totally convinced herself of it, right?
So she was desperate.
If she still hadn't found him by the time she graduated, she might have put out a nationwide call for him.
That way, there might be at least one, right?
Or she'd force some guy to change his name.
Ahahahaha...{p}

But you know, when Hirai became a third-year, he showed up.
Her destined one.
And at school, no less.
When that happens, you can't laugh off fortune-telling, can you?
It makes you feel like it really was a fated meeting.{p}Hey, hey, how do you think the person who fit all of Hirai's conditions perfectly showed up?
A new teacher
A transfer student
An incoming first-year
It was a teacher who'd just come to our school.{p}

He was fresh out of college, and kind of a dud, they say.
His hair was a shaggy mess, he wore glasses as thick as the bottom of a milk bottle, he was short and dumpy...
Basically, he looked like the kind of guy who'd never have a woman in his life.
Fate can be pretty cruel that way, huh?
If I were Hirai, I'd just decide on my own that the fortune was definitely wrong.
But you know, Hirai didn't care about looks.
Anyway, as long as his name and birthday and stuff were ideal, his looks and personality didn't matter at all, apparently.
I'd totally hate that, though.
The teacher's name was Shinji Kondo.
He doesn't live up to his name, right?
The name sounds so cool.
Hirai's heart started pounding, apparently.
She said there'd been five people so far with the same name.
But none of them had the birthday, the blood type and the birthplace that matched the fortune.{p}

So, heart pounding, she asked him.
"...Um, Mr. Kondo, please tell me your birthday, your blood type and where you're from."
She put her hands together and prayed to God.
Personally, I can't believe it.
Mr. Kondo was puzzled at first, but he told her right away.
And guess what?
It matched the fortune exactly!
You should have seen how happy Hirai was.
She said she saw a halo shining around Mr. Kondo.
But I mean, she'd finally met the person she'd been searching for all those years.
She must have been happy.{p}

From then on, Hirai stuck to Mr. Kondo like glue.
Everyone at school had heard the rumors about Hirai, so nobody was surprised.
But from Mr. Kondo's side, it was so sudden, right?
I mean, he had no idea at all that he was fated to marry Hirai.
Of course he was bewildered.
But you know, Mr. Kondo should've just been happy about it.
Because they say Hirai was really, really beautiful.
She was pretty, she had a great figure, and she'd told everyone she'd devote her whole life to serving her destined one, so for a guy, could anyone be better than that?
If I were a boy, I'm sure I'd have been happy.
Besides, a guy like Mr. Kondo could wait his whole life and no girl would ever come talk to him first.
He absolutely should have been thrilled.
But maybe Mr. Kondo had never been in love before.
Yeah, I bet that's it.
I mean, this gorgeous girl proposed to him, asking him to make her his bride, right?
He didn't know what to do.
So Mr. Kondo, get this, started avoiding Hirai.{p}

But maybe that's normal.
They were teacher and student, after all.
If anything went wrong, it'd be bad, and after he'd finally become a teacher, he'd get fired.
Besides, Mr. Kondo didn't believe what Hirai was telling him.
Well, I get that too.
A dreamy high school girl blurts out something weird on a passing whim.
It's like a sickness.
And once the sickness is cured, she's totally over it, like nothing happened.
"Huh? What was that about?"
Like that.
So if a guy gets ideas and tries to seriously go out with her... in the end, he's the one who ends up looking like a fool.
That kind of thing happens all the time, you know.
Besides, Hirai kept hanging around Mr. Kondo, so he got called in by the principal.
For Mr. Kondo, it might've been nothing but trouble.
So that's why he avoided Hirai.
But you know, Hirai wasn't the type to give up that easily.
Of course not.
I mean, he was her destined one.
Besides, if she couldn't be with him by twenty, she'd die.{p}

"Please! Stop joking around.
Do you enjoy tormenting me like this?
A girl like you, there must be plenty of other guys who'd want to go out with you, right?
Go find someone more suited to you."
That's what he said, crying and begging her.
"...Mr. Kondo.
Do you hate me?"
From Hirai's point of view, she couldn't understand why he was avoiding her.
He was the one she'd been waiting for all this time, so naturally, she thought he should feel the same way.{p}

"It's not a question of liking or hating.
You and I are teacher and student."
"Why can't a teacher and a student be together?"
"...Why?
That's just common sense.
There's my reputation, and how people would see it... it's just no good, that's all."
Mr. Kondo got kind of scared. He desperately bowed his head to her.
"...I understand.
Then once I've graduated, it's all right, isn't it?"
Hirai was actually pretty understanding.
Well, he was her destined one.
She couldn't go making trouble for him.
And even after high school, she'd still have time before she turned twenty.{p}

"...Uh, y-yes.
I suppose so.
If you graduate from high school properly, I'll give it some serious thought."
There was still almost a year until Hirai graduated.
With that much time, her feelings would surely change.
That's what Mr. Kondo thought.{p}

Hirai smiled, satisfied, and held out her right hand.
"...It's a promise, Mr. Kondo.
Pinky swear."
"...Uh, y-yes."
Mr. Kondo held out his right hand too, and they hooked their little fingers together in a pinky swear.
"Pinky swear, pinky swear, if you lie, you'll swaaaallow a thousand needles.
Finger cut!"{p}

After that, Hirai stopped following Mr. Kondo around, as if everything up to then had been a lie.
She threw herself into studying and went back to being a normal high school student.
To be exact, she pretended to be a normal high school student.
But you know, Mr. Kondo wasn't at ease at all.
Like, say some other girl went to ask Mr. Kondo a question or something.{p}

Then Hirai would be watching it all from the shadows, staring hard.
With the most terrifying look in her eyes.
You belong to me, Mr. Kondo.
If you lay a hand on another woman, I won't let it go.
That's what her eyes were saying.{p}

Around then, another teacher came to talk something over with Mr. Kondo.
"Mr. Kondo, there's a bit of a problem."
"What is it?"
"Well, it's about Hirai..."
Mr. Kondo had a bad feeling.
But so as not to let it show, he acted perfectly calm.
"What about Hirai?"
"Mr. Kondo, is something going on between you and Hirai?"
"...Meaning what?"
"Don't play dumb with me.
Hirai's saying she's going to marry you after she graduates.
So she says she won't take any college entrance exams, and she won't look for a job either.
At this rate, there's no way I can give her career guidance."
"No, that's just a passing fancy of hers..."
"...Mr. Kondo.
Didn't something happen between you and Hirai?"
The insinuation in that question made Mr. Kondo indignant.
"D-don't say such ridiculous things!
I don't feel anything for Hirai!
Whatever Hirai thinks, whatever she says, it has nothing to do with me!"{p}

He slammed the desk and jumped to his feet, shouting before he knew it.
Every teacher in the faculty room turned around to see what was going on.{p}

You should have seen her eyes then.
They say they were burning with hatred.{p}So what do you think Mr. Kondo did then?
He went after her
He explained to the other teachers
He pretended nothing had happened

"Hirai!"
Mr. Kondo shouted, not caring who was watching, and rushed after her.
I wonder what the other teachers thought.
I bet they got the wrong idea.
When you think about it, maybe the one you should really feel sorry for was Mr. Kondo.
Mr. Kondo chased her desperately, trying somehow to talk to Hirai.
But he was a slow runner.
Hirai, on the other hand, was a fast runner.
For Mr. Kondo, just keeping her in sight was the best he could do.
Somehow he managed not to lose her, but he couldn't close the distance at all.{p}

And once she ran into the gym, Hirai fell, way too obviously, as if she'd planned it from the start.
But thanks to her falling, Mr. Kondo was finally able to catch up.{p}

The empty gym was cold, and the air felt dead.
"Hirai.
Don't get the wrong idea.
I was only thinking of what's best for you...!"
Mr. Kondo grabbed Hirai's arm and forced her to turn around.{p}

Hirai's face was blank, cold as ice.
"...You lied, Mr. Kondo."
"I didn't lie!
I'm a teacher!
There's no way I can go out with you!"
Mr. Kondo pleaded desperately, his voice cracking.
But no matter what logic he twisted together, none of it got through to Hirai.
Mr. Kondo panicked.
But the more he panicked, the more it sounded like lame excuses, and the less convincing he got.
To Hirai, words like that didn't matter at all.
All she cared about was marrying Mr. Kondo.
"...You and I are tied together by the red thread, Mr. Kondo.
So you can't run away from it.
It's fate."
"...Hirai!
Please understand!
Don't make things any harder for me!
You can't believe in something you can't even see, like a red thread!"
"Don't be troubled, Mr. Kondo.
The red thread really does exist."{p}

There's no telling what a girl that desperate might do.
It wouldn't be strange if she killed him.
At that thought, he realized he was already starting to back away.
But you know, there's no way Hirai would attack Mr. Kondo, right?
I mean, he was the destined one she loved.
Hirai stabbed the knife she'd pulled out into the base of the little finger on her own right hand.{p}

"...Wh-what are you doing, Hirai?"
"...I'm going to show you the proof now.
Don't worry, my future husband."
Hirai smiled with only her mouth, her eyes still blank, and threw the knife away.{p}

Then she forced the wound she'd just made wide open and dragged the nerve out from inside.
"Ah... ah...ahh......ahhh..."
Each time the nerve, soaked bright red with blood, slithered out of her little finger, Hirai's face filled with rapture, and her whole body shook and convulsed.
"...See? The red thread."
And she showed it to Mr. Kondo, delighted.
Red blood was dripping from her little finger, drip, drip.
And that blood was running down along the nerve she'd pulled out, trickling slowly.
Mr. Kondo had no idea what to say, and could only open and close his mouth like a goldfish.{p}What do you think Mr. Kondo did?
He ran away
He fought with the dropped knife
He hugged Hirai without thinking

He forgot all about school.
He didn't even go back to the faculty room, he just ran all the way home.
But once he got back to his apartment, it hit him all over again.
Hirai knew where this apartment was.
It was right as he realized that.{p}

He heard a knocking at the door.
Mr. Kondo was so scared he covered his ears.{p}

But he could still hear it.
Hirai's voice crept in, slipping through the gaps in the hands pressed over his ears.
"...Hey, Mr. Kondo.
Why did you run away?
We're tied together by the red thread."
"No!
That's not true!"
Mr. Kondo forced himself to shout, trying to drown out Hirai's words.
But Hirai's voice seemed to echo right inside his head.
"...Mr. Kondo.
Do you remember the promise?
Our pinky swear."{p}

That moment came back to Mr. Kondo.
The pinky swear he'd made with Hirai.
"...Hey, Mr. Kondo?
You remember, don't you? Our promise.
The promise that you'd marry me once I graduated from high school.
Hey, Mr. Kondo, you remember, don't you?"
Hirai's voice didn't stop.{p}
And neither did the pounding on the door.{p}
What do you think Mr. Kondo answered then?
I remember.
I forgot.
Just go home!
Forgive me!

"I... I remember.
I remember, so please, have mercy on me!"
The instant he said it, the knocking on the door stopped.
And so did Hirai's voice.
Instead, he heard footsteps.
Footsteps moving away from the door.
As the footsteps faded, the terror that had hit its peak slowly died down too.
The footsteps were completely gone.
...What should I do?
Should I open the door and check?
That's what Mr. Kondo thought.{p}So, what do you think he did?
He opened the door to look
He didn't open the door

He shook his head and pushed the thought away.
She might still be on the other side of the door.
So he mustn't open it.
And so he waited until night came.{p}

He held his body rigid, held his breath, strained his ears so he wouldn't miss even the tiniest sound, and waited for dawn.
It was a long night.
Every second ticked off by the clock hands crawled by, like slow motion.
And at some point, Mr. Kondo fell asleep.
As time went by, the tension wore off and he let his guard down, you know.
But in the middle of the night, a suspicious noise woke him up.
Something was rustling around in the room.{p}

So he rubbed his sleepy eyes and took a good look, and guess what? Hirai was standing right in front of him.
Mr. Kondo was wide awake in an instant, but no voice would come out.
"...Mr. Kondo.
I have a spare key, so I let myself in.
I'm so glad you remembered our promise, Mr. Kondo.
The promise that you'd swallow a thousand needles."{p}

In the dim light he couldn't see Hirai clearly, but the big bowl she held was glittering.
That bowl was heaped with glittering silver needles.
Mr. Kondo had no time to think.
Hirai grabbed Mr. Kondo's upper lip and yanked it up as hard as she could.{p}

"...Here you go, a thousand needles.
Chew them well, chew them well, and eat lots and lots.
My beloved future husband."
Once she'd poured in every needle, she closed his mouth and worked his jaw up and down.
So he could chew them properly.{p}

"Mngh... hagh..."
The needles packed in his mouth burst through the flesh of his cheeks, and red needles came poking out.
Even so, Hirai showed no mercy.
Over and over she worked his jaw, and made sure he ate every last one, nice and clean.
By then, Mr. Kondo had gone quiet, too.{p}

"What's wrong?
Did you fall asleep already?
And here I was, about to show you how the two of us are tied together by the red thread..."
Murmuring that, Hirai opened the limp Mr. Kondo's mouth and peered inside.
"...Oh my, you haven't eaten them all yet.
Leaving so many behind... What a naughty boy."
Countless needles were stuck all over the inside of his mouth.
His tongue, especially, was bristling with them.
Hirai pulled out one of the needles.{p}

Then she bit off Mr. Kondo's right little finger and pulled out a single nerve.
After that, using the needle, she deftly stitched the nerve she'd drawn out of her own little finger to the nerve she'd drawn out of Mr. Kondo's.
"...See? We're tied together by the red thread.
Your little finger and my little finger.
...Right?"
Hirai, who had kept her face blank the whole time, smiled for the very first time.
And then she buried her face in Mr. Kondo's needle-stuffed belly and fell asleep.{p}

...These days, I hear Hirai lives in a hospital.
She seems perfectly normal, apparently.
My big sister's been to visit her a few times, so she knows.
And it was on one of those visits that Hirai told her this story.
My sister's seven years older than me.
She's twenty-three now.
She works in an office.
But Hirai, who was in her year, is still nineteen.
She says she'll be nineteen forever and never get any older.
'Cause if she turned twenty, she'd die.
Hirai herself believes that, so there's nothing anyone can do, right?
So her family keeps telling her she's still nineteen, forever and ever.
And apparently they're searching really hard.
Searching for who, you ask?
Isn't it obvious?
Someone named Shinji Kondo.
Mr. Kondo died, remember?

So unless they find a replacement Shinji Kondo, Hirai can't get any older.
Umm, what were his birthday and blood type again?
I did hear them, but I forgot.
But at this point, does that even matter anymore?
If her family can just find somebody close enough, they'll cover for it somehow.
...Though if Hirai ever found out, she might kill him.
Hey, hey, if you have a friend named Shinji Kondo, would you tell me?
I'll introduce him to her.
Don't worry, it'll be fine.{p}

Oh, I know!
What about you, {a}?
Don't worry, if we play it smart, she won't find out.

If you find someone good, you want to get married soon, right?
And Hirai's really beautiful, you know.

Oh, right, looks don't matter to you, do they, {a}?
What matters is personality, right?
Don't worry, Hirai has a really great personality.
After all, she's the type to devote herself to one man.
And she says she's learning to cook, too.
Anyway, she's got all the time in the world.
She's nineteen forever, after all.{p}

And that's the end of my story, but...
...The seventh one still isn't here, huh.
What should we do?
Should we just go home?{p}

Hmm.
I guess boys aren't really into that kind of stuff.
Then you don't believe in fortune-telling either, do you?
Thing is, there are lots of girls who get totally hooked on that stuff.
And apparently something scary happened once because of it.
...That's the kind of story I'm going to tell.{p}

Hmm.
...So you want to get married soon, huh.
Wow.
...
But that doesn't mean just anyone will do, right?
Anyway, about Hirai, who I was telling you about.{p}

I told you she wanted to get married really, really badly, right?
Well, apparently her standards were ridiculously high, too.{p}

Hmm.
...Is that really true?
Aren't you just playing the lone wolf because you're not very popular?
Oh, kidding, kidding.
Don't get mad.
Anyway, about Hirai, who I was telling you about.{p}

Huh, so you like pretty women after all.
I wonder if all boys are like that.{p}Okay, so what's your next priority?
Personality
Housework in general

Personality, huh.
Well, once you're married, you have to make it work together forever.
If your personalities don't click, there's nothing you can do.
...And housework comes dead last.
Yeah, that makes sense.
Even if someone's not much good at that stuff when they get married, they'll probably get better at it as they go.
But hey, so looks are your number one priority, {a}?
With a face like that, you're picky about looks? Who knew.{p}

Pfft.
Oh, no, it's nothing.
Ahaha!
No, no, don't mind me.
...Sorry, I need to get on with the story.
It was about Hirai, right?{p}

Hirai was a real beauty, I hear.
But that's not all.
She was lively and cheerful, so she was pretty popular.
And she loved fortune-telling.
She was the president of the Fortune-Telling Club.{p}

She was pretty, and she had a great personality, too.
Well, I don't know about her housework.
But since she wanted to get married so badly, she could probably manage some of it, right?
...Even if she wasn't all that good at it.
Anyway, Hirai was really popular with boys.
Apparently quite a few boys joined the club just because of her.
It seems guys confessed to her a lot and stuff, but...
Her standards were super high, remember?
So she turned down all kinds of people.
Her ideal guy was good-looking, smart, aiming for a good university...
Well, actually, that wasn't the kind of guy she wanted.
She said her ideal was someone who would understand everything about her.
That's all.
But that's really hard, isn't it?
Just by being a boy and a girl, you think in fundamentally different ways.
And yet, someone who understands every single thing about her...
You just don't come across people like that, right?
That's why people said her standards were super high.
But you know what?
There was someone like that.
A boy who made her think, "He's the one who'll understand everything about me."{p}

His name was Hiromichi Sato.
He was a boy who joined the Fortune-Telling Club partway through his first year.
Unlike the boys who were after Hirai, he joined because he was actually interested in fortune-telling.
He was a really kind person, it seems.
And he was the type who noticed all sorts of things.
Like, "In a situation like this, something like that might happen later," or "If you do this, it'll probably turn out like that."
He was really good at seeing that kind of thing.
You could say he had sharp instincts, or that he was just smart...
That's why Sato was good at fortune-telling, too.
Everyone said his readings were spot-on.
He could tell fortunes, and he was good at reading people's feelings...{p}

When she saw Sato, she thought he was the one, no question about it.
So she'd go up and talk to him and all.
And she'd be nice to him in all sorts of ways.
And Sato wouldn't mind having a pretty senior in his club be nice to him, right?
The two of them got closer and closer.
They'd shared a hobby, fortune-telling, from the start, so they never ran out of things to talk about.
Like a new kind of fortune-telling, or a fortune-telling shop they'd found.
Which fortune-teller was amazing, or what the fortune-telling machine at the arcade was like.
They talked about all kinds of stuff, it seems.{p}

But there was something fundamentally different about the two of them.
Hirai loved fortune-telling because she believed in mystical powers.
Sato loved fortune-telling because he was interested in reading people's minds.
...That was the difference.
Do you get what that means?
Hirai was a romantic, but Sato was a realist.
Sato understood that.
When you tell someone's fortune, you ask them all sorts of questions as you go, right?
Their name, their blood type, their star sign.
Whether they like someone, whether they have any worries...
Then, from their answers and gestures, their looks and their tone of voice, you make all kinds of judgments and come up with a result, apparently.
Sato was really interested in that kind of back-and-forth.
And since he was really good at it, his fortunes often came true.{p}

But Hirai was different.
She purely believed in the mystery of fortune-telling.
Sato knew the two of them saw things differently.
So he never tried to talk with Hirai about how they each saw fortune-telling.
He didn't want to wreck what they had by arguing over something like that.{p}

But Hirai...
She never noticed that fact.
When she saw Sato's fortunes come true, she simply looked up to him.
